title: Test agents, MCP and the CLI (AI-assisted testing)
summary: Playwright ships agent definitions (planner, generator, healer) via `npx playwright init-agents`, a bundled MCP server (`npx playwright mcp`), and `playwright-cli`. 1.64 adds WebMCP testing.
why: AI assistants can draft test plans and tests and propose fixes — useful for speed, but a QA engineer still decides what is worth testing and reviews every assertion.
body:
Verified in the official release notes:
• Playwright Agents (v1.56): planner explores the app and writes a Markdown test plan; generator turns it into tests; healer runs tests and proposes repairs. Set up with npx playwright init-agents --loop=vscode|claude|codex|copilot|opencode.
• Playwright MCP (bundled since v1.62): npx playwright mcp starts the Model Context Protocol server so an AI client can drive a browser through accessibility snapshots; playwright-cli (v1.58+) offers a token-efficient command mode.
• v1.64: page.webmcp / frame.webmcp test the tools a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API; Playwright MCP exposes them as webmcp_<tool>.
Treat generated tests like codegen output: review locators, add meaningful assertions, check they fail when the app is broken (the gate in this lab does exactly that with planted bugs).
objectives: Know what init-agents, mcp and cli provide
pitfalls: Accepting generated tests that assert nothing meaningful.
Letting a 'healer' change assertions to match a real bug.

example.code:
npx playwright init-agents --loop=vscode   # planner / generator / healer definitions
npx playwright mcp                          # bundled MCP server
npx playwright cli --help                   # agent-friendly CLI
